messages.subject: vector*Matrix*vector problem
parts:
Hello!

Im having some trouble multiplying vector*matrix*vector. I want to multiply the gradient with the inverse hessian and then multiply it again with the gradient (this is correction term when you don't evaluate the likelihood in optimum for the Laplace approximation). I have tried all the different combinations I can think of and I always get an error. One example is given below. It is the last term of the last equation I can't make sense of. 

  matrix<Type> H = autodiff::hessian(f,x);
  vector<Type> g = autodiff::gradient(f,x);
  vector<Type> tmp = atomic::matinv(H)*g;
  Type res = Type(0.5)*atomic::logdet(H) + f(x) + g.transpose()*atomic::matinv(H)*g;
  return res;

Any tips are much appreciated! 

Best regard, 
Jens

parts:
Could the issue be that

g.transpose()*atomic::matinv(H)*g

is in fact a 1-by-1 matrix, so on should do

(g.transpose()*atomic::matinv(H)*g)(0)

to get a Type ?

messages.author: ad9c431a7c6afc6f
messages.subject: Re: vector*Matrix*vector problem
parts:
Thank you! This solved the final step in the problem.

The problem seems to be that taking the transpose of a vector doesn't do much. I therefore made the gradient into a 1xn matrix, then took the transpose of this and multiplied it together in two steps and then applied your answer, and this compiles.

matrix<Type> H = autodiff::hessian(f,x);
  vector<Type> g = autodiff::gradient(f,x);

matrix<Type> g_mat = g.matrix();
  matrix<Type> tmp = g_mat.transpose()*atomic::matinv(H);
  matrix<Type> tmp2 = tmp*g;
  Type res = Type(0.5)*atomic::logdet(H) + f(x) + (tmp2)(0);
  return res; 

I have added below the program I used to do the testing on a nxn matrix and 1xn vector: 

  DATA_MATRIX(X); 
  DATA_VECTOR(z); 
  matrix<Type> tran = z.matrix();
  matrix<Type> trans = tran.transpose();
  matrix<Type> trans_z = trans*X; // Returns 1xn matrix. Need to be matrix<Type>, vector<Type> crashes
  matrix<Type> trans_zz = trans_z*z; // 1x1 matrix. One can also use vector<Type>
  REPORT(trans_zz);
  Type test2 = (trans_zz)(0); //Transforms from 1x1 matrix to Type
  REPORT(test2);
 
 Any comment on how to do this more efficient is appreciated! 
Jens
